builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Latent Merger: Latent-Space Composition of Hypernetwork-Generated LoRAs
summary: Latent-space LoRA merging replaces storing one LoRA adapter per document by composing the hypernetwork's intermediate latents and decoding them into a single fixed-rank adapter. It costs a dependency on an existing hypernetwork pipeline (Doc-to-LoRA or SHINE) and its frozen generation head, adding no serving-time memory beyond one adapter but requiring the hypernetwork infrastructure to be trained and maintained. It can fail because the approach depends on the specific spectral structure of hypernetwork-generated LoRAs, so gains may not transfer to directly fine-tuned adapters, and the abstract reports only qualitative improvements without quantified retention of per-document knowledge.
rationale: The method is only relevant if the reader already deploys a hypernetwork-based doc-to-LoRA system, and the unquantified improvement over simpler merging baselines requires validation on their own document stream.

claims.statement: Latent-space LoRA merging replaces storing one LoRA adapter per document by composing the hypernetwork's intermediate latents and decoding them into a single fixed-rank adapter. It costs a dependency on an existing hypernetwork pipeline (Doc-to-LoRA or SHINE) and its frozen generation head, adding no serving-time memory beyond one adapter but requiring the hypernetwork infrastructure to be trained and maintained. It can fail because the approach depends on the specific spectral structure of hypernetwork-generated LoRAs, so gains may not transfer to directly fine-tuned adapters, and the abstract reports only qualitative improvements without quantified retention of per-document knowledge.
Latent-space merging is reported to consistently improve over weight-space and factor-space merging baselines while preserving a single fixed-rank adapter; no quantified magnitude is given.
